abort_rule.rule: A row whose baseline route aborts at the memory cap (every route runs under ulimit -v 8000000, in kB; abort = the CLI process ends by SIGABRT, exit status -6 in Python's subprocess, or its log has Rust's 'memory allocation of <n> bytes failed'; the exit status and the log are kept) counts as the fix's win if the fix arm completes on that row (exit 0, a session written) without a hard-guard breach. With no baseline to anchor option (b), the hard guards on such a row are raw: via_in_pad_raw 0 (no via in an SMD pad that the input has no via for) and the router's clearance_violations 0; below_minimum_raw is reported, not judged (the router's pin neck-down puts copper under the class width by design, N06.4 amendment 2). The row's totals contribution (the fix's unrouted) is reported but not gated. A fix arm that aborts or fails on any row, a baseline that fails in any other way, or an aborted-baseline row whose fix breaks a guard, is a fail of the verdict
abort_rule.runner: tools/bench/n06_run.py with abort_rule: a route of a listed arm that aborts as defined above is logged in summary.json (exit, aborted, alloc_failure) and the run goes on; any other failed route stops the run as before

pairs_rule: The verdict pair (baseline, fix): first the abort rule on every row whose baseline aborted; then freerouting-dev gate --prereg docs/roadmap/prereg/N06.16.json --rows <every row whose baseline did not abort> judges the totals block with the hard and guard metrics on those rows (via_in_pad and below_minimum no new breach versus baseline, option (b); clearance_violations not above the baseline's). The verdict passes when both pass. On the identity rows (fixtures/Issue026-J2_reference.dsn, fixtures/Issue143-rpi_splitter.dsn, fixtures/Issue508-DAC2020_bm08.dsn and the two -90 variants) both arms must show session_differences 0 and any_angle_room_side_mismatches 0; either failing is a bug in N06.16's reach claim, not a verdict

boards.eligibility: every row; no row is dropped after a number. Chosen before any routed number under this registration: every any-angle variant in crates/freerouting/tests/data/autoroute-variants/*-any.dsn (J2-any, rpi_splitter-any, scoring-mixed-layer-any: the rows where the switch is reached), the 45 degree originals of the two boards that blow up plus Issue508-DAC2020_bm08 (small), and the two 90 degree variants, as identity checks: the counter only fires in the any-angle neighbour calculation, which the autoroute uses only with the plain search tree (SortedRoomNeighbours.selectCalculationMode; crates/freerouting/src/autoroute/session/mod.rs select_calculation_mode), and the autoroute tree is the plain one only when the board has no trace angle restriction (board/search/mod.rs get_autoroute_tree), or a net routes in the default tree's clearance class 0. N06.16's note does not state this; the identity rows check it

metric_definitions.via_in_pad: no new breach versus baseline (option (b), N06.4 amendment 2): the arm's count of vias in an SMD pad that the input has no via with that centre, padstack and nets for, minus the baseline arm's on the same row, floored at 0; raw count via_in_pad_raw. One measuring tool on the engine at 08062e2 for both arms (the input's session wiring stripped before the SES is imported, the SES read at the writer's scale)
metric_definitions.below_minimum: no new breach versus baseline (option (b)): the arm's delivered traces narrower than the board's narrowest class width that the input does not have, minus the baseline arm's, floored at 0; raw count below_minimum_raw; the same tool
metric_definitions.clearance_violations: the router's clearance violations of the final board (result.json board_statistics)
metric_definitions.unrouted: connections.incomplete_count of the final board (result.json board_statistics); the totals signal
metric_definitions.aborted: 1 when the arm's route aborted at the memory cap (abort_rule), else 0
metric_definitions.session_differences: n06_run.py: 1 when the arm's SES differs from the baseline's (or either has none)
metric_definitions.any_angle_room_side_mismatches: STATS total.counts.any_angle_room_side_mismatches (N06.16's counter, both arms): neighbour calculations whose room has more border lines than its simplex
metric_definitions.peak_rss_kb: the route's peak resident set (n06_run.py: os.wait4's ru_maxrss of the route; Linux counts the forked runner's image before exec, so its floor is the runner's own resident set, about 17 MB)

paired_rule_note: pass_rule is retained for gate parser validation; the registered verdict uses totals with accept=no-regress and the abort rule
keep_rule: N06's accept rule for (b) fixes: accepted when the abort rule holds on every aborted-baseline row, and on the other rows the hard guards hold, no board regresses by more than twice its noise band and the total is not worse than the set's noise; a neutral fix stays in. accept: The switch's tests (N06.16's done note) pass at the engine.
On the identity rows both arms' sessions are identical and the counter is 0.
Every aborted-baseline row passes the abort rule.
The other rows pass the totals rule (no-regress) with the hard and guard metrics.
stop_rule: one registered run per arm per board; no reruns with other settings
orchestrator: Build the release CLI from the worktree; from the worktree root run orchestrator_command (n06_run.py honours abort_rule and records peak RSS; it exits non-zero when sessions differ, after writing summary.json); run the measuring tool on each SES; build records with every row (an aborted baseline's metrics null); apply the abort rule by script; judge the other rows with freerouting-dev gate --prereg docs/roadmap/prereg/N06.16.json --rows <those rows> (baseline file first with --write-baseline)
